stories.headline: TSMC Q1 Profit Jumps 58% to Record on AI Boom; 2nm Enters Volume Production

key_facts.fact: TSMC reported Q1 2026 revenue of NT$1.134 trillion, up 35.1% year-over-year, and net profit of NT$572.48 billion, up 58.3% YoY — both records beating consensus
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC's Q1 2026 revenue hit a record $35.6B, up 35% YoY, driven by AI chip demand and 5-10% price hikes on advanced processes.

key_facts.fact: Gross margin expanded to 66.2% (up 390 basis points sequentially) and operating margin hit 58.1%, both exceeding the high end of TSMC's guidance
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC achieved a gross margin of 66.2% and an operating margin of 58.1%, both exceeding the high end of its expectations… Revenue of $35.9 billion, exceeding guidance.

key_facts.fact: CEO C.C. Wei said 2nm (N2) has entered volume production with good yield and is stepping up capex on 3nm, and told analysts customers reassured AI demand was still strong despite the Iran war
key_facts.excerpt: TSMC lifts full-year outlook above 30% as AI demand powers another record quarter… second-quarter guidance that signals the AI-driven chip boom is accelerating rather than plateauing.

key_facts.fact: 3nm accounted for 25% of wafer revenue in Q1, and chips 7nm or smaller represented roughly 74% of wafer revenue
key_facts.excerpt: Strong demand for 3-nanometer technology… 3-nanometer process, which accounted for 25% of wafer revenue.

key_facts.fact: TSMC guided Q2 2026 revenue of $39.0B-$40.2B (about 10% sequential growth) and reiterated roughly 30% full-year USD revenue growth on a 2026 capex plan of $52-56 billion
key_facts.excerpt: The company's previous guidance for 2026 calls for approx. 30% USD revenue growth and capex of $52–56 billion… Bank of America, Goldman Sachs, and JP Morgan all expect management to reiterate these key figures.

stories.headline: Spain's $90B Aragón Data Center Buildout Draws AWS, Microsoft — and Local Resistance

key_facts.fact: Bloomberg reported northern Spain's Aragón region is absorbing roughly $90 billion of data-center investment that Big Tech wants to hold up as a model for the EU, while locals fight forced land sales and worry about water shortages
key_facts.excerpt: Big Tech companies say northern Spain's AI buildout is going so well, it should be a model for other parts of the EU… A data-center buildout in the Spanish region of Aragón has divided locals and regional officials.

key_facts.fact: At Zaragoza's 'The Wave 2026' conference on April 14, AWS Spain chief Suzana Curic said the company has committed €33.7 billion to data centers and a server factory in Aragón, covering campuses across all three provinces (Zaragoza, Huesca and Teruel)
key_facts.excerpt: ha reivindicado el papel de la multinacional en Aragón, con una inversión comprometida de 33.700 millones en centros de datos y una fábrica de servidores… 'Somos la primera empresa que va a estar presente en las tres provincias'

key_facts.fact: Microsoft Spain CEO Paco Salcedo said at the same conference that Microsoft will start work this year on its Aragón campuses at La Muela, Villamayor and Puerto Venecia, with more than €8 billion in committed investment
key_facts.excerpt: la intención del gigante estadounidense es empezar las obras de sus campus en Aragón (La Muela, Villamayor y Puerto Venecia) este mismo año, con una inversión comprometida que cifra en más de 8.000 millones de euros.

key_facts.fact: Local resident Paz Orge Acebillo told Bloomberg her family received a letter on behalf of AWS offering a 'private amicable agreement' to buy land her family had owned for 50 years, giving them four days to respond, under a government 'general interest' designation
key_facts.excerpt: Paz Orge Acebillo's family received a letter on behalf of Amazon Web Services proposing a 'private amicable agreement' to buy the land her family had owned for nearly half a century… The letter cited a government-backed data-center project labelled 'of general interest.'

stories.headline: Unitree Sells $8,150 Humanoid Robot on AliExpress, Aiming Squarely at Tesla's Home Market

key_facts.fact: On April 15, Hangzhou-based Unitree Robotics began international sales of its R1 humanoid robot on Alibaba's AliExpress platform, priced at about $8,150 including import fees (roughly $6,800 for a scaled-down version), with free shipping to the US
key_facts.excerpt: Hangzhou-based Unitree's R1 model will cost roughly US$8,150 with import fees factored in, and shipping to the US will be free of charge, the company said on Wednesday. It will also offer a scaled-down version priced at about US$6,800.

key_facts.fact: Distribution targets the US, Canada, Japan, the UAE and Singapore, via AliExpress, and is positioned as an aggressive move into Tesla's home market while Optimus remains in development
key_facts.excerpt: The R1 robots will be sold to markets including the US, Canada, Japan, the United Arab Emirates, and Singapore via AliExpress… It is an aggressive move to seek out customers in Tesla's home market, at a time when the US company is still developing its Optimus humanoid product line.

key_facts.fact: Unitree shipped around 5,500 humanoid robots in 2025, mostly to universities and research labs, and saw revenue surge more than 300% last year according to its IPO prospectus
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree sold some 5,500 humanoid robots in 2025, mostly to universities and research labs. Rising demand both at home and abroad for its bipedal and quadruped robots has fueled a more than 300% surge in revenue last year, according to the company's IPO prospectus.

key_facts.fact: The rollout precedes Unitree's planned 4.2 billion yuan IPO on Shanghai's STAR Market; Chinese makers led global humanoid shipment volumes in 2025, outpacing Tesla and Figure AI per research firm Omdia
key_facts.excerpt: Unitree's partnership with Alibaba… comes ahead of a 4.2 billion yuan (S$783.3 million) initial public offering on Shanghai's Nasdaq-like Star Market… Chinese robot makers led global shipment volumes in 2025, far outstripping US rivals including Tesla and Figure AI, according to research agency Omdia.

key_facts.fact: Alibaba this week announced plans to develop its own four-legged robot to compete with Unitree's Go line, even as it hosts Unitree's international launch
key_facts.excerpt: Alibaba, for its part, this week announced that it too is getting into the robotics arena with plans to develop and sell its own four-legged robot, which would compete with Unitree's Go series.

stories.headline: US Energy Agency Will Force Data Centers to Disclose Nationwide Power Use

key_facts.fact: In an April 9 letter seen by WIRED, the US Energy Information Administration told Senators Josh Hawley and Elizabeth Warren it plans to implement the first-ever mandatory nationwide survey of data centers focused on their energy use
key_facts.excerpt: The US federal government's central energy information agency is planning to implement a mandatory nationwide survey of data centers focused on their energy use, according to a letter seen by WIRED. This survey would be the first effort of its type to collect basic information about data centers.

key_facts.fact: The commitment follows a March letter from Hawley and Warren pressing EIA to cover an industry consuming ever-increasing amounts of power; EIA has not set an implementation date
key_facts.excerpt: The development comes a month after Sens. Josh Hawley and Elizabeth Warren sent a letter asking the EIA to gather data on data centers… The nationwide survey will be mandatory, Wired reports. The agency has not yet set a date for when it will implement the new questionnaire.

key_facts.fact: EIA ran a pilot survey of 196 companies in Texas, Washington state and the D.C.–Northern Virginia metro area in March, plans a second pilot in three other states in April, and expects both to wrap in September before building the mandatory questionnaire
key_facts.excerpt: The EIA announced in March that it would conduct a pilot survey of 196 companies in Texas, Washington state, and the Washington, D.C.-Northern Virginia metro area, and in April it said it would launch a second survey in three different states. EIA chief Tristan Abbey expects the two pilot surveys to be complete in September.

key_facts.fact: The move comes as 27 states advance data-center bills requiring developers to cover energy costs and report usage, and Maine prepares to become the first state to implement a statewide data-center moratorium through November 2027
key_facts.excerpt: Twenty-seven states are advancing state data center legislation that requires developers to cover data center energy costs and report usage, with California, Ohio, and Utah already enacting laws… Maine is poised to become the first state to implement data center construction moratoriums, pausing new projects until November 2027.

stories.headline: Amazon-Backed X-Energy Launches IPO Targeting Up to $7.5B Valuation to Power AI Data Centers

key_facts.fact: X-Energy, a developer of small modular nuclear reactors, announced April 15 that it had launched the roadshow for its IPO of 42,857,143 shares of Class A common stock, to list on the Nasdaq Global Select Market under the ticker 'XE'
key_facts.excerpt: X-Energy, Inc. ('X-energy'), a leader in advanced nuclear reactor and fuel technology, today announced the launch of the roadshow for its initial public offering ('IPO') of 42,857,143 shares of its Class A common stock… X-energy's Class A common stock has been approved for listing, subject to official notice of issuance, under the ticker symbol 'XE' on the Nasdaq Global Select Market.

key_facts.fact: The Amazon-backed, Maryland-based company is targeting up to a $7.51 billion valuation and aiming to raise up to roughly $814.3 million, pricing shares at $16–$29 (initial range disclosed as $16–$19 per share in its launch release)
key_facts.excerpt: X-Energy, backed by Amazon, said Wednesday that it aimed to achieve a valuation of up to $7.51 billion in its initial IPO in the United States. The Maryland-based nuclear reactor developer is looking to raise up to $814.3 million by selling approximately 42.9 million shares at a price between $16 and $29.

key_facts.fact: J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Jefferies and Moelis & Company are the lead joint book-running managers for the offering
key_facts.excerpt: J.P. Morgan, Morgan Stanley, Jefferies, and Moelis & Company are acting as the lead joint book-running managers for the offering.

key_facts.fact: X-Energy's flagship Xe-100 SMR uses helium rather than water as a coolant, and its Triso-X fuel subsidiary received a February license from the US Nuclear Regulatory Commission to manufacture commercial reactor fuel in Tennessee
key_facts.excerpt: The company is building a reactor called Xe-100 that uses helium instead of water as a coolant. The U.S. Nuclear Power regulator granted a license in February to Triso-X a subsidiary of X-Energy to manufacture a fuel for commercial reactors at a plant in Tennessee.

key_facts.fact: Reuters/Morgan Stanley estimate global electricity demand will grow more than one trillion kWh per year through 2030, with data centers contributing nearly 20% of that growth — the thesis underpinning the SMR revival
key_facts.excerpt: Morgan Stanley says that global electricity demand is expected to increase by more than one trillion kWh per year through 2030. Data centers are expected to contribute to nearly 20% of the growth.

stories.headline: Amazon Signs Record 9 Australian Renewable PPAs Totaling 430 MW to Feed AI Cloud Buildout

key_facts.fact: Amazon Australia announced on April 15 the signing of nine new power purchase agreements across New South Wales and Victoria, adding 430 MW of wind, solar and battery storage capacity at a cost of roughly A$2.8 billion
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon Australia announced the huge 430 megawatt (MW), $A2.8 billion buy-up on Wednesday, with eight of the nine deals incorporating battery storage – and three of those projects being utility-scale solar-battery hybrids – a first for Amazon outside of the United States.

key_facts.fact: Eight of the nine deals incorporate battery storage, and the three utility-scale solar-battery hybrids are Amazon's first such hybrid projects outside of the United States
key_facts.excerpt: Eight of the nine deals incorporate battery energy storage systems —Amazon's first solar-battery hybrid projects in Australia, and the first outside the United States.

key_facts.fact: The portfolio includes a 201 MW offtake from Tag Energy's Golden Plains wind farm in Victoria, plus solar-battery hybrids at OX2's Muswellbrook project (94.5 MW PV + 70 MW battery), X-ELIO's Forest Glen (72 MW PV + 72 MW battery) and Anza Power's Laceby (48 MW each)
key_facts.excerpt: The three large-scale solar-hybrid PPAs include 94.5 MW of PV and 70 MW of battery capacity from OX2's Muswellbrook project in New South Wales coal country, 72 MW each of PV and battery from X-ELIO's Forest Glen project near Dubbo in NSW, and 48 MW each from Anza Power's Laceby project near Wangaratta in Victoria.

key_facts.fact: The deals bring Amazon's Australian renewable portfolio to 20 projects with a combined 990 MW of capacity, on top of an estimated A$2.8 billion already invested since 2020, and AWS says the storage focus is meant to prove data centers 'can run confidently on an increasingly renewables-based system'
key_facts.excerpt: As we expand our cloud and AI infrastructure, we're powering it not only with carbon-free energy, but also battery storage that strengthens grid reliability and proves data centres can run confidently on an increasingly renewables-based system.

stories.headline: China's 2025 Chip-Tool Imports Surged Via Singapore and Malaysia as Direct US Shipments Hit 8-Year Low

key_facts.fact: A Nikkei Asia analysis published April 15 found China's semiconductor manufacturing equipment imports from Singapore and Malaysia hit record levels in 2025, surpassing direct shipments from the US, which sank to an eight-year low
key_facts.excerpt: China's imports of chipmaking equipment from Malaysia and Singapore rose sharply in 2025 to surpass those from the U.S., which sank to an eight-year low, a Nikkei Asia analysis has found -- yet American companies remain a vital source of advanced tools for the country.

key_facts.fact: Chip-tool imports from Singapore rose 17% year-on-year to $5.7 billion in 2025, while imports from Malaysia more than doubled to $3.4 billion, and direct US imports fell 34% to roughly $2 billion
key_facts.excerpt: China chip tool imports shift to Southeast Asia as US tightens export controls… China's imports of semiconductor manufacturing equipment from Southeast Asia surged in 2025, surpassing direct shipments from the US, according to a Nikkei Asia analysis.

key_facts.fact: The rerouting lets Chinese firms obtain tools from Applied Materials and Lam Research via third-country intermediaries at a 25-40% premium, while direct US sales to China decline but 'Other Asia' sales grow
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese firms are bypassing US export controls by routing advanced semiconductor manufacturing equipment through Southeast Asian intermediaries, specifically in Malaysia and Vietnam… Regulatory Arbitrage: China is leveraging 'third-country' hubs to acquire tools from Applied Materials (NASDAQ: AMAT) and Lam Research (NASDAQ: LRCX).

key_facts.fact: A separate Reuters report on April 14 said China's largest NAND maker YMTC plans two additional fabs beyond one wrapping this year, collectively more than doubling its 200,000-wafer-per-month capacity, with over 50% of equipment for the new facility sourced from domestic suppliers like AMEC
key_facts.excerpt: Chinese chipmaker Yangtze Memory Technologies (YMTC) aims to build two more factories in addition to one that will be completed this year, which will more than double its production capacity… adding that more than 50% of equipment has been sourced from domestic companies including critical tools used for vertical stacking of chip layers.
